doc.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Feeling 6/8 against duple rhythms
summary: The 6/8 feel of Rumba Colombia, with quinto and clave in two, and how long it took Rendón to understand.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: The rhythms that really got my heart going yesterday were those 6/8 things. And I think it’s such a powerful feeling because you can feel it in two, you can feel it in six, and you can move your body in different ways to it.

Like we did “Rumba Colombia” [scats] 1-2-3-4-5-6; 1-2-3- 4-5-6. But then the quinto player is going [scats]. It’s like a different improvisation, it’s in two, it’s just in duple feel against the 6/8. And also we have the clave [scats] I can do the other part instead of doing this [scats]. That’s in two. So you have all this interplay and it’s really interesting. And again, it took me a long time to really understand it, because my mind wouldn’t accept it, being a schooled musician.
